properties.biography: Formed in 1992 by Isaac Brock, Jeremiah Green and Eric Judy in Issaquah, Washington, Modest Mouse emerged from the same Pacific Northwest indie community that produced numerous influential alternative acts. The band released early lo-fi records and EPs before achieving wide critical acclaim with The Moon & Antarctica (2000), produced by Phil Ek, which showcased more expansive production and complex arrangements. Their 2004 album Good News for People Who Love Bad News delivered a wider commercial breakthrough, propelled by the single "Float On," while retaining the band's idiosyncratic lyrical voice. Over decades the lineup shifted frequently around Brock; members and collaborators expanded the band's sonic palette with horns, keyboards and varied percussion. Modest Mouse maintained credibility in indie circles while achieving mainstream exposure through radio, TV placements and festival appearances. Founding drummer Jeremiah Green died in 2022, but the band's recordings and influence continue to resonate across indie and alternative rock.
properties.known_for: Idiosyncratic, guitar-driven indie rock that mixes lo-fi and experimental textures with introspective, often ironic lyrics and Isaac Brock's distinctive vocal delivery.
properties.description: Modest Mouse is an American indie rock band formed in 1992 in Issaquah, Washington. Led by singer-songwriter Isaac Brock, the group is known for jagged, textured guitars, inventive arrangements, and often existential, wry lyrics. They rose from the 1990s Pacific Northwest indie scene to international recognition with critically acclaimed albums such as The Moon & Antarctica (2000) and mainstream breakthrough Good News for People Who Love Bad News (2004), which included the hit single "Float On." Their sound blends lo-fi and experimental elements with melodic songwriting and angular instrumentation.
properties.cultural_impact: Modest Mouse helped bridge 1990s indie credibility with 2000s mainstream alternative success, influencing the sound and aesthetic of many post-2000 indie rock bands. Their single "Float On" became a widely recognized anthem, increasing indie music's radio presence. The band's distinctive voice and songwriting have been referenced across media, and their albums are commonly cited in discussions of turn-of-the-century indie rock evolution.
properties.performance_style: Live shows mix tight, melodic passages with loose, improvisatory sections; Isaac Brock often engages the audience with conversational between-song remarks, and the band can switch from subdued atmosphere to loud, chaotic climaxes.

properties.biography: Born in Queens, New York in 1970 and raised largely in Los Angeles, John Frusciante rose to prominence after joining the Red Hot Chili Peppers in 1988. His guitar work helped define the band's breakthrough sound on albums such as Mother's Milk and Blood Sugar Sex Magik. After leaving the band in the early 1990s he pursued a solo career marked by experimental, lo-fi and electronic releases, struggled publicly with addiction, then recovered and rejoined the Chili Peppers in 1998. Frusciante contributed to several of the band's most successful albums (including Californication, By the Way and Stadium Arcadium), left again in 2009 to focus on solo and electronic music, and returned to the band in 2019. Outside the band he has released numerous solo albums and collaborated with artists and groups such as Ataxia and Omar Rodríguez-López.

properties.biography: Formed in London in 1999 by vocalist Kele Okereke and guitarist Russell Lissack, Bloc Party rounded out its classic lineup with bassist Gordon Moakes and drummer Matt Tong. After a string of acclaimed early singles and EPs they released their debut album Silent Alarm in 2005, produced by Paul Epworth; it earned wide critical praise and commercial success and established them at the forefront of the post-punk revival. Subsequent albums — A Weekend in the City (2007), Intimacy (2008), Four (2012), Hymns (2016) and Alpha Games (2022) — saw the band experiment with electronic production, dance-punk rhythms and more reflective songwriting. Lineup changes in the 2010s (Tong and Moakes departing; Justin Harris and Louise Bartle joining) preceded further stylistic shifts, but the band has retained its reputation for taut, danceable guitar-driven rock and high-energy live shows.

properties.biography: Formed in Sheffield in 2002 when school friends Alex Turner (vocals/guitar), Jamie Cook (guitar), Matt Helders (drums) and Andy Nicholson (bass) began playing local shows, Arctic Monkeys built an early audience through demo CDs, word-of-mouth and MySpace. Noted for witty, observational lyrics and propulsive guitar-driven arrangements, the band has evolved across albums—from raw garage/indie rock to moodier, art- and lounge-inflected records such as AM and Tranquility Base Hotel & Casino—while maintaining strong commercial and critical success worldwide.

properties.biography: Formed in Middletown, Connecticut, while Andrew VanWyngarden and Ben Goldwasser were students at Wesleyan University, the duo initially recorded as The Management and released early demos (later leaked as Climbing to New Lows). They changed their name to MGMT, signed first to Cantora Records and then to Columbia Records after their Time to Pretend EP drew wider attention. Their 2007 debut Oracular Spectacular made them international stars with anthems that married indie-pop songwriting to retro-futuristic synth textures. With Congratulations (2010) and the self-titled MGMT (2013) they pursued increasingly experimental directions, dividing critics and fans, before returning to a looser pop approach on Little Dark Age (2018). After leaving Columbia in 2019 they released music independently, took an informal hiatus, and returned with Loss Of Life (2024), which introduced more contemporary production and their first-ever guest feature. Throughout their career the duo have remained the creative core, supported live and in the studio by a rotating band of collaborators and touring members.

properties.description: MGMT is an American psychedelic rock and synthpop duo formed in 2002 at Wesleyan University by Andrew VanWyngarden and Ben Goldwasser. They rose to international prominence after signing to Columbia Records and releasing their breakthrough debut Oracular Spectacular (2007), which included the hits "Time to Pretend", "Kids" and "Electric Feel". Subsequent records—Congratulations (2010), MGMT (2013), Little Dark Age (2018) and Loss Of Life (2024)—showcase a progression from accessible synth-pop to more experimental psychedelia and back toward a contemporary pop-inflected sound. The core duo write and perform with a rotating cast of touring/studio members; MGMT are noted for blending lush harmonies, surreal lyrics and synth-driven arrangements while maintaining a strong visual and live-theatrical presence.
properties.cultural_impact: MGMT helped bring psychedelic textures and synth-driven production into mainstream indie in the late 2000s; their early hits became cultural touchstones of the era and influenced a wave of indie and synth-pop bands. They are also notable for polarizing critical debate when they shifted toward more experimental material, demonstrating that commercially successful indie acts could pursue avant-garde directions and still retain a dedicated audience.

properties.biography: Formed in Dublin in 1983 by Kevin Shields, Colm Ó Cíosóig and David Conway, My Bloody Valentine relocated to London early in their career and went through several lineup changes before stabilizing with Kevin Shields, Bilinda Butcher, Colm Ó Cíosóig and Debbie Googe. Their early releases and EPs led to the full-length Isn't Anything (1988), which established their gliding, heavily processed guitar sound. Loveless (1991) is widely regarded as a production and artistic milestone — recorded over protracted sessions with exhaustive experimentation — but legal and financial issues contributed to a lengthy band hiatus from the mid-1990s. They reunited in the 2000s, toured intermittently, and self-released m b v in 2013. The band is renowned for pioneering techniques (notably Kevin Shields' 'glide guitar') that shaped shoegaze and influenced generations of alternative and experimental artists.

properties.description: My Bloody Valentine are an Irish-English alternative rock band formed in Dublin in 1983 and later based in London. They are best known for creating dense, effect-heavy guitar textures, pioneering the shoegaze sound on landmark releases such as Isn't Anything (1988) and Loveless (1991). Their music blends layered, reverb- and distortion-drenched guitars, blurred, breathy vocals, and unconventional production techniques. After a long hiatus in the mid-1990s the band reformed in the 2000s and released m b v in 2013, cementing their reputation as hugely influential figures in underground and indie music worldwide.

properties.biography: Metric began in 1998 when singer-songwriter Emily Haines and guitarist/producer James Shaw started collaborating in Toronto and Montreal after earlier work together and separate projects. The band expanded in 2001 with bassist Joshua Winstead and drummer Joules Scott-Key, and after delays released Old World Underground, Where Are You Now? (2003). Subsequent albums such as Live It Out (2005) and Fantasies (2009) cemented their status in the Canadian and international indie scenes. Members pursue side projects—Haines with solo work and Broken Social Scene; Winstead and Scott-Key as Bang Lime—while Metric maintain an active recording and touring career.

properties.description: Metric is a Toronto-formed Canadian indie rock and new wave band founded in 1998 by Emily Haines and James Shaw. The lineup solidified with Josh Winstead (bass, synths) and Joules Scott-Key (drums). They combine synth-driven textures with guitar-based indie rock and insightful, often introspective lyrics. Metric have released multiple acclaimed albums (notably Old World Underground, Where Are You Now?, Live It Out, Fantasies, Synthetica, Pagans in Vegas, Art of Doubt, Formentera and Formentera II), won Juno Awards including Group of the Year and Alternative Album of the Year, and built a strong international following through touring and sync placements in films and video games.
properties.cultural_impact: Metric helped define the Canadian indie rock resurgence of the 2000s, achieving domestic commercial success and international recognition. Emily Haines's presence and perspectives have also made the band an influential voice for thoughtful, female-fronted indie rock.
